title: Playing classical halls in Paris and the money
summary: He was the first jazz act booked by the Jeunesse Musicales, playing the Palais Chaillot and Olympia, with modest pay.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: It had always been classical until they booked me. And I played in places...I played in the Salle de Veaux in Paris? Do you know the Salle de Veaux? It's an exclusive, classical stronghold. I played in the Palais Chaillot, which is a huge place. I also played at the Olympia. I played the Salle Pleyal. And I did the Fair de Paris; the Radio Diffusion; I made a lot of records, you know. And enjoyed a very, very big success. Not moneywise, because they just don't give you a lot of money. You know. When you get...I guess the money and opportunities don't go together. If they give you what they call the break, then they give you one or the other.

And I...one of the things that has been so disturbing to me also, is that...take like a folk singer today, and guitar player. All he has is his guitar, harmonica and a chair and a microphone. They give him four hundred and fifty dollars a week or five hundred dollars a week, which is a good salary for a guy that ain't making no money. Now, they book him for twenty-one concerts. There's where he can stay fourteen to twenty-one days. All right? He play the concerts, they give him five hundred bucks and that's three weeks. And then he get right back on the plane and come back here. The impresario
is left with all the money. All he got was uppercuts and five hundred dollars.
